summary: Both round-2 items are genuinely closed, confirmed via live mutation testing, not eyeballing. (1) The 7-day backstop cutoff is now pinned: neutralizing `_set_overlap_backstop_verdict`'s cutoff comparison (news_bot.py, replacing `if not ts or str(ts) < cutoff:` with `if not ts:`) makes `test_backstop_excludes_candidate_older_than_7_days` (candidate aged to -10 days via direct `UPDATE published_articles SET published_at=...`) FAIL with `AssertionError: 0 != 1` while its companion `test_backstop_includes_candidate_within_7_days` (-3 days) stays green — exactly the asymmetric result a correct boundary pin should produce. news_bot.py was restored byte-for-byte afterward (md5 f130d920319dc42f4359e242823e2150 before and after). (2) The class-level `SOURCES` patch does target the right thing: `SOURCES` (news_bot.py:2058) is a list of direct function references built at import time, so `job()`'s `for fetcher in SOURCES:` loop only sees whatever list object is currently bound to the module attribute — patching the function name would not touch entries already stored in the list, so patching the list itself is required and correct. `TestCrossSourceDedup` (17 tests) is stable across 3 repeated runs and the full `tests/test_integration.py` suite (30 tests) is stable across 2 repeated runs, no flakes observed. However, while investigating item 2's 'properly scoped in setUp/tearDown' requirement, I found and empirically confirmed a NEW bug in the fix itself: the new `TestCrossSourceDedup.setUp`/`tearDown` (tests/test_integration.py:880-906) reuses the exact attribute name `self.sources_patcher` that the (pre-existing, unmodified-by-this-round) base class `_IntegrationBase.setUp`/`tearDown` (tests/test_integration.py:97-110) already uses for its OWN SOURCES patch. This shadows the base patcher's reference on `self`, so `_IntegrationBase.tearDown`'s `self.sources_patcher.stop()` silently no-ops (unittest.mock's `_patch.stop()` swallows the `ValueError` when the patcher is no longer in `_active_patches` and returns `None` without restoring anything) instead of restoring the true original `news_bot.SOURCES`. I verified this empirically: after running exactly one `TestCrossSourceDedup` test via unittest in a fresh interpreter, `news_bot.SOURCES` is permanently left mutated from the pristine `[_fetch_rss_entries, _fetch_orangetrack_entries]` to `[_fetch_rss_entries, _fetch_mattel_entries]` for the rest of the process, with one `mock._patch` object confirmed still sitting in the global `_active_patches` registry, never stopped. This does not currently break any assertion (repeated runs are green) because `fetch_mattel_news` is separately mocked to return `[]` and orangetrack was already excluded from `SOURCES` by the pre-existing base-class patch even before this round's change — meaning the new patch's own stated rationale ('job() otherwise also runs the live-network _fetch_orangetrack_entries source... NOT mocked here') is factually incorrect: orangetrack was already fully excluded for every `_IntegrationBase`-derived test, this class included, prior to this fix. The new patch is therefore solving a problem that (as diagnosed) did not exist at this call site, while introducing a real, verified test-isolation defect (leaked global mutable state + an un-stoppable base patcher) in the process — precisely the class of bug ('shared state', Category 6 anti-pattern) this fix was meant to prevent. It is inert today only because pytest is invoked fresh per command; a reordering, a new test added after this class in the same session, or a parallel/randomized test runner could surface it as real flakiness later.

findings.issue: TestCrossSourceDedup.setUp assigns `self.sources_patcher = patch('news_bot.SOURCES', [news_bot._fetch_rss_entries])` and starts it — reusing the identical attribute name the base class `_IntegrationBase.setUp` already uses for its own (different) SOURCES patch (`[_fetch_rss_entries, _fetch_mattel_entries]`). This overwrites the `self.sources_patcher` reference, so when `_IntegrationBase.tearDown` later calls `self.sources_patcher.stop()`, it is actually calling `.stop()` a SECOND time on the CHILD's patcher object (already stopped by the child's own tearDown one line earlier), which unittest.mock silently no-ops (catches ValueError on `_active_patches.remove(self)`, returns None). The base class's own patcher is never stopped. Empirically verified: after one TestCrossSourceDedup test runs (via a fresh interpreter, unittest runner), `news_bot.SOURCES` is left permanently mutated from the true original `[_fetch_rss_entries, _fetch_orangetrack_entries]` to `[_fetch_rss_entries, _fetch_mattel_entries]`, and `unittest.mock._patch._active_patches` retains one leaked, never-stopped patcher targeting `news_bot.SOURCES` for the rest of the process. Separately, the code comment's stated rationale for the patch ("job() otherwise also runs the live-network _fetch_orangetrack_entries source... NOT mocked here") is factually wrong: `_IntegrationBase.setUp` (pre-existing, not touched by this round) already excludes `_fetch_orangetrack_entries` from `SOURCES` for every test in this class both before and after this round's change, so the new patch cannot be the thing that fixed a live-network leak at this call site — whatever caused the round-2 flakiness (if genuinely observed), this patch does not address it, while it does introduce a fresh, verified isolation bug of its own. Currently inert (fetch_mattel_news is mocked to `[]` either way, so no assertion currently differs), but it is exactly the 'shared mutable state across tests' anti-pattern this round's fix was supposed to eliminate, and the misleading comment will send a future debugger down the wrong path.
findings.recommendation: Rename the class-level patcher to a name that cannot collide with the base class, e.g. `self.dedup_sources_patcher = patch('news_bot.SOURCES', [news_bot._fetch_rss_entries])`, and use that name in both setUp and tearDown (`self.dedup_sources_patcher.stop()` before `super().tearDown()`, same position as today). This lets `_IntegrationBase`'s own `self.sources_patcher` survive untouched and be correctly stopped exactly once by `_IntegrationBase.tearDown`, restoring the true original `news_bot.SOURCES` at the end of every test. Additionally, correct the setUp comment to state the real reason for the narrower list: to also exclude `_fetch_mattel_entries` (redundant with the already-mocked `fetch_mattel_news` return value, but keeps `SOURCES` minimal/obvious for this class), NOT to prevent a live orangetrack call that was already prevented by the base class. Re-run the empirical check after the fix: `python3 -c "import news_bot, unittest, tests.test_integration as ti; pristine=list(news_bot.SOURCES); unittest.TextTestRunner().run(unittest.TestLoader().loadTestsFromName('TestCrossSourceDedup.test_hard_block_path', ti)); assert [f.__name__ for f in news_bot.SOURCES]==[f.__name__ for f in pristine], news_bot.SOURCES"` — it should assert-pass (no mutation) once fixed.

roundTwoFindingsVerified.originalIssue: 7-day backstop cutoff (`_set_overlap_backstop_verdict`'s Python date-math replacing the old SQL-level `days=7` windowing) had zero boundary coverage; neutralizing the cutoff check left the whole suite green.
roundTwoFindingsVerified.verificationMethod: Live mutation test: changed news_bot.py:1057 from `if not ts or str(ts) < cutoff:` to `if not ts:` (removing the date comparison, so the backstop compares against ALL 30-day candidates instead of the intended 7-day subset). Ran the two new boundary tests: `test_backstop_excludes_candidate_older_than_7_days` (seed aged to `datetime('now','-10 days')`) FAILED with `AssertionError: 0 != 1 : candidate aged past the 7-day backstop window must NOT block` — the now-unfiltered 10-day-old candidate incorrectly hard-blocked the article. Its companion `test_backstop_includes_candidate_within_7_days` (seed aged to -3 days) still PASSED under the same mutation, confirming the pair isn't just accidentally always-blocking. Restored news_bot.py; md5sum before mutation and after restore both f130d920319dc42f4359e242823e2150 — diff is clean, no residual change. Full `TestCrossSourceDedup` (17 tests) and full file (30 tests) reconfirmed green post-restore.

roundTwoFindingsVerified.originalIssue: Class was network-dependent / flaky because job() allegedly also ran the live `_fetch_orangetrack_entries` source, unmocked, during TestCrossSourceDedup runs.
roundTwoFindingsVerified.verificationResult: partially resolved — patch target is correct, but scoping is broken (see new major finding above)
roundTwoFindingsVerified.verificationMethod: Confirmed `SOURCES` (news_bot.py:2058) is a plain list of direct function references consumed by `job()`'s `for fetcher in SOURCES:` (news_bot.py:2209), so patching the list (not the function name) is the structurally correct approach — patching `news_bot._fetch_orangetrack_entries` alone would not have changed entries already captured in the list. Ran `TestCrossSourceDedup` 3x and the full file 2x: 100% stable, zero flakes observed in this environment. However, tracing the setUp/tearDown scoping (as explicitly requested) surfaced that the class's own `self.sources_patcher` attribute collides with and shadows the identically-named attribute already used by the (pre-existing, untouched-by-this-round) `_IntegrationBase.setUp`/`tearDown`, so the base class's own SOURCES patcher is silently never stopped — see the new major finding for the empirical proof. Also found the patch's stated rationale is inaccurate: the pre-existing base-class patch already excluded `_fetch_orangetrack_entries` from `SOURCES` for this class both before and after this round's change, so orangetrack was never actually reachable here to begin with.

litmusTest.note: 2 boundary tests mutation-verified directly (both pass litmus: cutoff removal breaks exactly the -10-day test, not the -3-day companion). SOURCES-patch scoping is not a litmus-style logic test — it is a test-infrastructure isolation defect, reported separately as an anti_pattern finding rather than a litmus failure. Remaining 15 TestCrossSourceDedup tests were not re-mutated this round (news_bot.py unchanged since round 2, where they were already mutation-verified per test-reviewer-round2.json).
